paras: The 1919 Vernon Avenue boys' fight was a clash on Chicago's South Side on a Monday afternoon in early June 1919, in which white boys and white spectators attacked Black boys with bricks and stones. No one was reported killed or hurt, but police arriving on a riot call took several Black boys away in a patrol wagon. The Chicago Defender reported it as a "miniature Race riot" and contrasted its own boys with whites "of the ruffian type."

According to the Defender, the fight began shortly after school let out, when "certain white boys, laboring under the illusion that they were lords of creation," tried to take property from Alfred Thomson of 6818 Eberhardt avenue (one scan of the story reads "Thorp"). Alfred and his brother Arthur resisted, and the white boys took up bricks and stones and attacked them. Arthur's friends joined the defense and chased the white boys several blocks to 67th and Vernon avenue, where a crowd of nearly one hundred spectators was watching a ball game.

The spectators then joined the white boys, and by the paper's count twenty-five or thirty Black boys were in the fight as "stones and bricks were flying thick." Someone sent in a riot call, and a patrol wagon took away Arthur Turburn of Langley avenue, Willie McSee (or McSea) and Eddie Young. A fifth person from Eberhardt avenue, whose name is garbled in the printed text, was also taken at a woman's instigation.
No report of charges, a court hearing or the boys' release was found, and the Defender named no white boys as arrested.

The only known account is an unsigned local item on page 15 of the Chicago Defender of 7 June 1919, printed among community notes; no other paper was found to carry it. The paper took the Black boys' side throughout, calling the white boys "marauders" and describing the patrol wagon's arrival as "singularly and yet characteristic[ally]" done, an implied charge of one-sided policing. It closed by stating that the Black boys came from respectable families while the white participants "were of the ruffian type."

accounts.label: Black correspondent (Chicago Defender)
accounts.gist: White boys started the fight by trying to take a Black boy's property and attacking with bricks and stones; when chased, they called on about a hundred ball-game spectators, and police arriving on a riot call took away Black boys.

framing.detail: Local-news item calling it a 'miniature Race riot', mocking the white boys as 'lords of creation' and 'marauders', contrasting 'our boys' from respectable families with whites 'of the ruffian type', and implying the police took only Black boys 'characteristically'.
